- If a tool call outside the workspace still triggers an approval prompt, tell the user — do not try to work around the permission system.
- Tool-call paths must be ABSOLUTE (`/home/jmeyer/...`) — never `~` or relative `../`. The tools do not expand `~` (it becomes a literal sub-path) and `../` is rejected with "Invalid path format" before the permission layer.

reason: Issue B (path-access, part 2): intercept bad tool-call paths in the existing tool.execute.before hook and normalize ~ and relative ../ to absolute before opencode core's "Invalid path format" check fires. This is the "control over the opencode process" — rewrite output.args.filePath/path/file_path. Every rewrite logs to console.error so a test run proves whether output.args mutation actually reaches the tool (opencode #31680/#42409 report it sometimes does not). If mutation is a no-op, the AGENTS.md absolute-path note is the reliable fallback and this block is removed.

Root cause of the external-path failure: /home/jmeyer/projects/portal/opencode.json is a project-level config that OVERRIDES the global ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json. Its external_directory only listed portal/** and programmer-tools/**, so the global B fix (~/.config/nvim/**) never applied in the portal session. Adding .config/nvim, .config/opencode, and projects/opencode-manage (all absolute, matching the file's existing style) restores cross-project read/grep/emit access.

Phase 1 of the managed-fs work: the daemon becomes the enforcement boundary for reads. /v1/read resolves+normalizes the path, then gates it on the project's state.db folders table (project-internal = always allowed; external = must be covered by an approved folder row, most-specific match wins so avoid overrides approve). Returns line-numbered file content or a sorted directory listing. Fail-closed everywhere: no store/table means external reads are denied.
Wire the new /v1/read endpoint into Mount so it is registered alongside the other daemon routes.

Phase 1: a `read` tool that overrides opencode's built-in read by name. It only normalizes the path and proxies to the daemon /v1/read — no filesystem access, no secrets. Mirrors the built-in args (filePath/offset/limit) so existing model calls keep working.
Register the new read override tool. Adding `read: readTool(directory)` (same name as the built-in → takes precedence) plus its import.

Add a `restart` target so rebuilding + restarting the daemon is one command instead of three. Skips the slow sqlc/nvim-lint steps (no SQL added), rebuilds bin/manage, kills the stale daemon; ensureDaemon() respawns the fresh binary on the next read.

.PHONY: build sqlc migrate-down test tidy run restart nvim-lint

NVIM_LUA_DIR ?= $(HOME)/.config/nvim/lua

tidy:
	go mod tidy

sqlc:
	sqlc generate

nvim-lint:
	@command -v nvim >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "nvim is required for nvim-lint"; exit 1; }
	@find "$(NVIM_LUA_DIR)" -type f -name '*.lua' -exec nvim --headless -u NONE --clean {} -c 'lua assert(loadfile(vim.fn.argv(0)))' -c 'qa!' \;

run: build
	./bin/manage

# fast dev-loop rebuild + restart: skip the slow sqlc/nvim-lint, kill the
# stale process; ensureDaemon() respawns the fresh binary on the next read.
restart:
	go build -o bin/manage ./cmd/manage
	@pkill -f 'opencode-manage/bin/manage' 2>/dev/null || true
	@echo "→ manage daemon rebuilt + stopped — next opencode read spawns the fresh binary"

test: tidy sqlc nvim-lint
	go test -count=1 ./...

migrate-down:
	go build -o bin/manage-down ./cmd/manage-down || true

reason: Fix the pkill -f self-match: the pattern 'opencode-manage/bin/manage' appears in the recipe shell's own argv, so pkill SIGTERMs itself ("make: Terminated"). The [m]anage bracket makes the pattern match the daemon process but not the shell running it.

reason: Nvim-side daemon lifecycle helper: shells out to `make -C <dir> restart` (no shell interpolation via the list form) and reports success/failure through vim.notify. MANAGE_DIR env overrides the default ~/projects/opencode-manage.
content:
-- /home/jmeyer/.config/nvim/lua/opencode-manage/daemon.lua FINAL
-- Manage daemon lifecycle. The daemon (Go, ~/projects/opencode-manage) is the
-- read/write enforcement boundary; the Makefile `restart` target rebuilds it
-- and kills the stale process, and the opencode plugin's ensureDaemon() then
-- respawns the fresh binary on the next tool call. This module just shells
-- out to `make restart` and reports via vim.notify.
local M = {}

local function default_dir()
	return (vim.env.HOME or "") .. "/projects/opencode-manage"
end

--- Rebuild + restart the manage daemon. Blocks until `make restart` returns.
--- Returns true on success. Feedback is vim.notify (INFO on success, ERROR on failure).
function M.restart()
	local dir = vim.env.MANAGE_DIR or default_dir()
	if vim.fn.isdirectory(dir) ~= 1 then
		vim.notify("manage daemon: " .. dir .. " not found (set MANAGE_DIR?)", vim.log.levels.ERROR)
		return false
	end
	vim.notify("manage daemon: rebuilding + restarting…", vim.log.levels.INFO)
	local out = vim.fn.system({ "make", "-C", dir, "restart" })
	if vim.v.shell_error == 0 then
		vim.notify("manage daemon: rebuilt ✓ — next opencode read spawns the fresh binary", vim.log.levels.INFO)
		return true
	end
	vim.notify("manage daemon: restart failed:\n" .. vim.trim(out), vim.log.levels.ERROR)
	return false
end

return M

reason: Register :ManageDaemonRestart so rebuilding/restarting the daemon is one command from inside nvim with vim.notify feedback.
